label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: logs COMPLETE, timings COMPLETE, handler max 605.148 ms, failures 0

report.summary: Outbox publication throughput fell to about 13 per 10 s against 34 arrivals per 10 s, building a backlog of up to 250 and delays of up to 73 s. Slow consumer handling in some deliveries fits, but the link is not proven.

findings.claim: Outbox publishing fell behind arrivals mid-window, growing pending to 250 and oldest undelivered age to 73 s; late notifications match this.
findings.reason: Arrivals stayed at 34 per 10 s while publications fell to about 13 per 10 s; pending and oldest age rose.

findings.claim: The transfers API itself was healthy, with no errors and stable latency, and no deliveries failed.
findings.reason: All 680 requests returned 201 with p95 0.241 s. All 570 delivery attempts succeeded and the failed count stayed 0.

findings.claim: A slow consumer handler on some deliveries is the likely cause: handler time reached about 605 ms against a p50 of 0.014 ms.
findings.reason: The slow tail is consumer-side, and serial delivery in batches of 20 per 1 s poll would cap throughput. The slow attempts were not matched to the slow buckets.

findings.claim: The database pool and locking are not the cause.
findings.reason: No pool acquisition timeouts or pending borrowers, and no blocking in any of the 100 samples.

limitations: Delivery log listing covers only the earliest 100 of 570 records, so the slow attempts are not tied to the throughput-drop period.
Attempt records (570) differ from the attempts reported by poll batches (585), and the consumer is a test fixture, so the slow handler may not reflect production.
next_checks: Align per-attempt handler duration with the 10 s publication buckets, especially 15:41:10 to 15:43:00.
Inspect the outbox publisher poll loop timing and thread state during the slowdown and recovery.

alternatives.reason: No publisher thread or poll-loop evidence was collected, and the recovery to about 80 per 10 s is unexplained.
alternatives.hypothesis: Publisher polling stalled or was throttled by something other than consumer latency, such as a scheduler pause.

alternatives.reason: The pool never saturated and no blocking was sampled, though sampling is coarse.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database contention or pool exhaustion delayed outbox reads.

A.rule: throughput shortfall without a slow consumer component

report.summary: Outbox publications dropped below the arrival rate and a backlog built, with the oldest undelivered event reaching 73 s. The consumer handler became slow (~605 ms) in some attempts, which fits a serialized publisher.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog grew because publications fell to ~13 per 10 s while arrivals stayed at 34 per 10 s; the oldest undelivered event reached 73 s.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show the drop from the sixth bucket onward, with pending rising from 2 to 250 and oldest age reaching 73 s.

findings.claim: Late notifications are not caused by the transfer API, delivery failures, DB pool exhaustion or DB blocking.
findings.reason: Transfers are all 201 with p99 0.25 s. Failed count is 0 and all 570 delivery attempts succeeded. The pool shows no pending borrowers or timeouts, and no DB blocking was sampled.

findings.claim: The consumer handler's slow tail (p95 605 ms, max 605 ms) lengthens delivery time to ~680 ms. If deliveries are serial, that caps throughput near the observed ~13-15 per 10 s.
findings.reason: Handler time is ~0.014 ms at p50 but ~605 ms at p95, while auth is a steady ~70 ms. The throughput arithmetic assumes serial delivery, which is not directly observed.

limitations: The delivery log lists only the earliest 100 of 570 records, which predate the slowdown, and poll batches report 585 attempts against 570 records.
The consumer is a test fixture, and there is no publisher thread or concurrency data or timeline of when the handler became slow.
next_checks: Correlate per-attempt handler latency with time to confirm the slow handler starts at the same time as the publication drop.
Inspect the outbox publisher's concurrency and poll loop, and explain the 15-attempt gap between the 585 poll-reported attempts and the 570 attempt records.

alternatives.reason: No publisher-side timing or concurrency data was collected.
alternatives.hypothesis: The publisher poll loop or batching is the limit (1 s poll, batch of 20), independent of consumer slowness.

alternatives.reason: The last three buckets show 75-82 publications per 10 s and pending falling to 115, consistent with recovery.
alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer slowness was transient and the backlog drains once it ends.
